observation.visible_scene: Interior view of a brightly lit carousel under an ornate gold canopy studded with small lights and decorated with painted panels on the central drum. Several painted horses (white with pink floral trim, purple, pink, yellow, teal, and a glossy blue winged horse) carry riders: a woman in a pale blue dress and straw hat seated on the white horse, a person in a striped shirt with a blue cross-body bag standing on the pink horse gripping the overhead pole, a woman in black overalls seated on the yellow horse, and a person in a white shirt seated on the blue winged horse. Other riders are partly visible in the background.
visible_changes: The carousel rotates continuously, so the near-side horses and riders translate horizontally across the frame (left to right) throughout the excerpt; motion is already underway at the first frame and does not stop at the last.

The pink horse with the standing striped-shirt rider, and the yellow horse with the black-overalls rider, drift rightward and leave the frame; the blue winged horse with the white-shirt rider enters from the left and moves toward the center.
The white horse with the seated woman in the blue dress travels from the left portion of the view toward the center and then rightward, keeping her seated grip on the pole.
The standing rider on the pink horse holds his raised-arm, foot-on-stirrup pose unchanged until the pair exits the view.

The central drum's painted panels shift rightward more slowly than the outer horses, and the foreground gold support poles sweep steadily rightward, consistent with rotation about a central axis rather than a pan of the whole scene.
Horses show slight changes in leg posture and height between frames, suggesting gentle up-and-down motion, though this is subtle.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the ride started or stops within this segment (the excerpt is a temporal crop with motion ongoing at both ends).
What lies beyond the left and right edges of the frame and the full rotation cycle.
The identities or actions of riders outside the visible field.
uncertain_details: Exact camera behavior: the steady rightward drift of foreground poles and outer horses is consistent with a stationary camera viewing a rotating carousel, but whether the camera is fully fixed or partly co-moving cannot be confirmed from the background alone.
The precise magnitude of vertical bobbing of the horses is hard to separate from perspective changes caused by rotation.

may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
